Topic: Someone in Northern Ireland loses £250,000 to an AI deepfake investment scam
Caption Notes:
Someone in Northern Ireland lost £250,000 to a scam that started with an AI-generated video of a well-known finance personality.

The video was only the hook. The rest happened on WhatsApp and on a laptop the scammers took control of.

4 warning signs:
1. A famous face promoting an investment
2. A small first payment, then pressure to pay more
3. The chat moves to WhatsApp
4. Someone asks for remote access to your computer

Spot one? Stop. Check the firm on the FCA register before you send a penny.

Police say a celebrity endorsement never proves an investment is real. Send this to someone who'd trust that video.

Source: PSNI, 7 Sep 2026.

Topic: UK small business AI use has more than doubled this year, to 47%
Caption Notes:
47% of UK small business owners now use AI. A year ago it was 22%.

Writing content, solving problems and coming up with ideas top the list. The confidence lags behind: fewer than 1 in 5 feel very confident using it, and security worries hold plenty back.

Using AI but not sure you're doing it right? Our starter guides cover the basics. Link in bio.

Source: Simply Business SME Insights Report 2026, survey of 1,842 UK small business owners.

Topic: Nearly half of UK adults find it harder to tell what's genuine online, NTS warns
Caption Notes:
Nearly half of UK adults (47%) say it’s getting harder to tell what’s genuine online. As AI grows, almost a quarter (24%) feel overwhelmed by how sophisticated scams have become.

National Trading Standards has published an AI Scam Watchlist of the top five AI-powered tricks: fake websites, voice cloning, deepfake video, AI-generated images and ‘digital humans’.

Bad spelling and blurry photos used to give scams away. They don’t anymore. Stop and think before you pay or share anything. Check the caller, website or message through a separate route, even if an AI search result says it’s real. Send no money and share no details until you’re confident.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: National Trading Standards, 30 Sep 2026.
